Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ## output_rules.md ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md — detailed inline comment files"] O4["Always reference inline comment files via the 'comment' field — do NOT use inline 'body'"] O5["Inline comments MUST use a line number that exists in the PR diff"] O6["If a finding is on unchanged code outside the diff, put it in outputs/pr_review_general.md instead"] O1 --> O2 --> O3 --> O4 --> O5 --> O6 ``` ## formatting_rules.md ```mermaid flowchart TD F1["outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief Markdown summary, under 20 lines, bullet-focused"] F2["Required sections: Summary, Key Issues, Next Steps"] F3["outputs/pr_review.json — valid JSON with recommendation, summary, inlineComments, issueCounts"] F4["Each inline comment: path, line, startLine, side, comment, severity (BLOCKING|IMPORTANT|SUGGESTION)"] F5["comment must be a path to a file under outputs/pr_review_comments/.md"] F6["outputs/pr_review_general.md — max 1-2 paragraphs, factual, no essays"] F7["If ci_failures.md present → include each failure as 🚨 BLOCKING (full logs in ci_failures_full.log)"] F8["Keep summary under 2 sentences — put details in inline comment files, not in general text"] F9["Severity classification follows general_guidelines.md:
BLOCKING = must fix · IMPORTANT = should fix · SUGGESTION = optional"] F10["Ticket context: verify PR changes satisfy ticket ACs — note gaps in review"] F11["Inline comments MUST target a line that appears in the PR diff
If the line is not in the diff, the comment becomes a general PR comment instead of a review thread"] F12["Use line numbers from the right-hand side of diff hunks
If pr_diff.txt is truncated, run git diff origin/{base}...HEAD to see the full diff"] ``` ## few_shots.md Example PR review outputs — keep concise: ### outputs/pr_review.json ```json { "recommendation": "BLOCK", "summary": "SQL injection in UserService.js must be fixed before merge.", "generalComment": "outputs/pr_review_general.md", "inlineComments": [ {"path":"src/auth/UserService.js","line":45,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","severity":"BLOCKING"}, {"path":"src/auth/LoginController.js","line":78,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","severity":"IMPORTANT"}, {"path":"src/utils/validation.js","line":23,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md","severity":"SUGGESTION"} ], "issueCounts": {"blocking":1,"important":1,"suggestions":1} } ``` ### outputs/pr_review_general.md ```markdown ## Automated Code Review — BLOCK **Summary**: SQL injection blocks merge. One important issue (weak password validation) and one suggestion (extract duplicated validation). **Next Steps**: 1. Fix SQL injection in UserService.js — use parameterized queries 2. Strengthen password validation (8+ chars, mixed case, numbers, symbols) 3. Extract shared email validation utility ``` ### outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md ```markdown 🚨 **BLOCKING: SQL Injection** User input is interpolated directly into the query at `UserService.js:45`: ```javascript const query = `SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '${email}'`; ``` Use parameterized queries instead: ```javascript const query = 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?'; await db.query(query, [email]); ``` ``` ## review_verdict_rules.md # Review verdict rules — machine protocol (binding) The review↔rework loop is a machine, not a conversation: your `recommendation` in `outputs/pr_review.json` is parsed mechanically and drives issue labels, rework runs and CI (each wasted round costs 15–20 CI minutes — gh-71). These rules govern the verdict; every other instruction (severity definitions, output files, thread etiquette) is unchanged. ## Verdict mapping Classify findings exactly as instructed: - 🚨 **BLOCKING** — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing gates (red CI), scope violations, security issues, data loss. - ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability debt worth fixing, but the PR works as shipped. - 💡 **SUGGESTION** — style, wording, import order, dartdoc refs, polish. Then map to the verdict: | Findings | `recommendation` | |---|---| | Any 🚨 BLOCKING (correctness/bug) | `REQUEST_CHANGES` — or `BLOCK` for security / data loss | | No 🚨 BLOCKING — only ⚠️ / 💡 remain | `APPROVE` | `APPROVE` with remaining ⚠️/💡 findings is the expected terminal state (`allowApproveWithSuggestions: true`): post every remaining finding as before (inline threads + general comment) — they do **not** block the merge and must **not** trigger another rework round. ## Anti-patterns (observed live, gh-71) - ❌ Returning `REQUEST_CHANGES` because a re-review surfaced new suggestion-level nits (docs wording, import style, dartdoc refs). A cycle with only suggestion-level findings **must** converge to `APPROVE`. - ❌ `REQUEST_CHANGES` while `issueCounts.blocking` is `0` — the machine treats that as an approval and skips the rework round. Keep `issueCounts` accurate: it is the machine's source of truth, not prose. The machine also cross-checks the counter against your inline comments (a `severity: "BLOCKING"` entry or a 🚨 marker in the referenced comment file) before honoring a blocking-0 approval — if any finding is truly blocking, set `recommendation: REQUEST_CHANGES` with `blocking: 1`+. - ❌ Verdict-by-prose: never phrase the verdict only in the summary text. The `recommendation` field of `outputs/pr_review.json` is the verdict. - ❌ 🚨 BLOCKING driven by an uncited external-spec claim ("the spec says X" without a `file:line` / doc URL the leg actually read). Downgrade it to a ⚠️ question; the machine treats BLOCKING threads as ground truth and arms rework on them. (Note: the post-action also downgrades such findings mechanically — keep the JSON consistent with the demoted severity so the census cross-check stays clean.) - ❌ Re-opening a thread that the rework demonstrably fixed in this diff — add its id to `resolvedThreadIds` instead. ## Label guard rails — the chore:pin lane (live: fa pr-1104, 2026-09-30) `chore:pin` is a trusted, **non-exclusive** factory fast-lane: several PRs may carry it at the same time (a release bump `chore/release-vX.Y.Z` AND a factory pin `chore/factory-pin-*` are both legitimate holders — they ride the lane independently). Reviews must therefore: - ❌ **NEVER remove `chore:pin` from any PR** — not as a "one pin" dedup, not as a side-effect of closing a related PR as superseded. Removing it from the release bump stranded the v1.0.494 tag behind the guest queue for an hour (fa pr-1104, unlabeled 13:31:08Z while pr-1105 was closed). - ✅ When a PR is superseded (e.g. a workflow change already shipped via another PR), close **only that PR** and leave every label on every other PR untouched. Label restoration is a keeper action, not yours. - ✅ If you believe two `chore:pin` holders conflict, SAY SO in the review comment and keep both labels — the owner resolves the lane, the machine only merges. ## github_comment_format.md # GitHub tracker comment Use GitHub-flavored Markdown in `outputs/response.md` for GitHub issue comments and descriptions. Your output is posted to the issue as-is — every construct must render natively on GitHub. - Headings: `##`, `###` - Bullets: `- item` - Numbered lists: `1. item` - Bold: `**text**` - Inline code: `` `code` `` - Code block: ` ```lang ... ``` ` with a language tag (`dart`, `bash`, `json`) - Link: `[text](url)` - Tables: standard GFM table syntax (`|---|` separator row) Do not use Jira wiki markup in GitHub fields: no `{code}...{code}` blocks, no `{panel}` macros, no `h1.`/`h2.`/`h3.` heading prefixes, no `{{monospace}}` inline code, no `[title|url]` links. None of it renders on GitHub — a comment full of `{code}` fences and `h3.` headers is unreadable. **IMPORTANT** When the issue references a parent story or related issues, get them for full context using: `dmtools github_get_issue OWNER/REPO#NUMBER` (the composite key form works directly). ## dmtools_cli.md ## DMTools CLI — External Data Access > **PR Review note**: Ticket/PR context is pre-loaded. Use dmtools only for additional data (e.g., parent story details, linked tickets not in input/). The `recommendation` field of `outputs/pr_review.json` is the verdict. - ❌ 🚨 BLOCKING driven by an uncited external-spec claim ("the spec says X" without a `file:line` / doc URL the leg actually read). Downgrade it to a ⚠️ question; the machine treats BLOCKING threads as ground truth and arms rework on them. (Note: the post-action also downgrades such findings mechanically — keep the JSON consistent with the demoted severity so the census cross-check stays clean.) - ❌ Re-opening a thread that the rework demonstrably fixed in this diff — add its id to `resolvedThreadIds` instead. ## Label guard rails — the chore:pin lane (live: fa pr-1104, 2026-09-30) `chore:pin` is a trusted, **non-exclusive** factory fast-lane: several PRs may carry it at the same time (a release bump `chore/release-vX.Y.Z` AND a factory pin `chore/factory-pin-*` are both legitimate holders — they ride the lane independently). Reviews must therefore: - ❌ **NEVER remove `chore:pin` from any PR** — not as a "one pin" dedup, not as a side-effect of closing a related PR as superseded. Removing it from the release bump stranded the v1.0.494 tag behind the guest queue for an hour (fa pr-1104, unlabeled 13:31:08Z while pr-1105 was closed). - ✅ When a PR is superseded (e.g. a workflow change already shipped via another PR), close **only that PR** and leave every label on every other PR untouched. Label restoration is a keeper action, not yours. - ✅ If you believe two `chore:pin` holders conflict, SAY SO in the review comment and keep both labels — the owner resolves the lane, the machine only merges.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1770._

> ℹ️ **8 resolved thread(s) excluded; 13 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `ContextWindowRegistry.remove` has no unit test at the seam**

The new per-identity drop (`context_window_registry.dart:145`) is only exercised end-to-end through the caps-flow test. Every other registry behavior has a direct unit test in `test/compaction/context_window_registry_test.dart` (`publish`, last-wins, identity keys, non-positive rejection). A three-line unit test — publish for an identity, `remove`, assert `windowFor` is null and `isVerified` is false — would keep the new API's contract pinned where the rest of the seam's contract lives, including that `remove` on an unknown identity is a no-op.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

🚨 **BLOCKING: unpinning the context window leaves a STALE userPin in the shared window registry — children and the meter keep the removed value**

The publish is conditional on the pin existing:

```dart
if (_pinnedCaps(provider, modelId)?.contextWindow != null) {
  contextWindowRegistry.publish(
    model: _agent.state.model,
    window: caps.contextWindow,
    source: ContextWindowSource.userPin,
  );
}
```

But `ContextWindowRegistry` is publish-only — later publishes win, there is no unpublish (`clear()` is documented as a test seam; "a host never calls this mid-session — E4 window shrinks arrive as new publishes"). So:

1. Pin `contextWindow: 1048576` on the active model → registry gains `userPin: 1M` (invariant 2: main, children, meter resolve ONE window).
2. Unpin it (thinking `off` row, or Remove this override) → the model is rebuilt from the catalog value, but the conditional above is now false → **nothing republishes and nothing drops the entry**.
3. Every child spawned afterwards (`withRegisteredContextWindow`) and the ctx meter (`windowFor(model) ?? model.contextWindow`) keep resolving **1M**, while the main model carries the catalog window — exactly the stale-window divergence gh-1742 built the registry to kill.

The same staleness hits the pin-only-on-maxTokens case in the new code path: an earlier `endpointReport` entry for the identity survives the rebuild even though the rebuilt main model no longer carries that value (see also the missing-endpoint-layer issue in the rebuild itself).

Fix: on unpin, publish the newly resolved window (the E4-shrink pattern), or add an unpublish/drop API to the registry and call it here. A regression test: pin window → unpin → assert `contextWindowRegistry.windowFor(model)` matches the rebuilt model (or is null).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the "full constructor" is not full — `maxImages` is dropped from the rebuilt ACTIVE model**

The comment above this block claims it "enumerates every field", but the `Model(` rebuild stops at `timeoutScopeLabel` and never passes `maxImages`:

```dart
_agent.state.model = Model(
  id: current.id,
  ...
  streamIdleTimeout: current.streamIdleTimeout,
  timeoutScopeLabel: current.timeoutScopeLabel,
  // maxImages: missing
);
```

`Model.maxImages` is the per-model unique-image ceiling the catalog carries (`catalogMaxImages`, e.g. `gemini-4-argon: 10`, issue #1750) and the image registry + agent loop read it off the live model (`agent_loop.dart: catalogMaxImages: config.model.maxImages`; `image_registry.dart: catalogMaxImages ?? imageRegistryConfig.maxPerRequest`). After ANY capability pin on a catalog model with a declared ceiling, the rebuilt model carries `maxImages: null` and the ceiling silently widens to the global `images.maxPerRequest` default — a field loss the retired `/model-edit` flow never caused (it copied via `copyWith`, which preserves `maxImages`).

The codebase's own live-rebuild precedent in this same directory does carry it: `_handleModelSwitch` passes `maxImages: catalogMaxImages[modelId]` when rebuilding on `/model <name>`.

Fix: `maxImages: catalogMaxImages[modelId]` (mirroring the boot build), and please extend the new live-apply test to assert the rebuilt model still carries the catalog image cap.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

💡 **SUGGESTION: not canonical dartfmt — the file's formatter would rewrite the new `testWidgets` header**

The new test header uses the pre-tall-style shape:

```dart
testWidgets('/model-edit → Model capabilities flow (merged surface)',
    (tester) async {
```

`dart format` (the same version that formats the rest of this file — main's copy is format-clean) rewrites it to the tall style every other long header in this file already uses (see the `/settings → provider → Edit picker` test above):

```dart
testWidgets('/model-edit → Model capabilities flow (merged surface)', (
  tester,
) async {
```

Understandable on a pure-`dart` host with no Flutter SDK (this leg can only be gated by the owner's flutter CI — locally `flutter test` also needs the gitignored `[REDACTED:Credential File]` asset), but since CI owns this file, may as well land it pre-formatted.

---

**vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit** (2026-10-22):

**vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit** (2026-10-22): Fixed in a1287ece02: `ContextWindowRegistry.remove(model)` added (per-identity drop, documented against the clear()-test-seam seam), and the apply path now keeps the registry in agreement with the rebuilt model in BOTH directions: pin (or roles-chain pin) → publish userPin; a still-winning endpoint detection → republish endpointReport; bare unpin → remove — children and the meter fall back to the rebuilt model's carried window. Regression test: `unpinning drops the stale userPin from the window registry` (pin via seed, remove via flow, asserts windowFor(model) is null). --- **vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit** (2026-10-22): Fixed in a1287ece02: the rebuild passes `maxImages: catalogMaxImages[modelId]` (the same source `_handleModelSwitch` and `buildCatalogModel` read). The "full constructor" comment now says "incl. the catalog image cap". Regression test: `the live rebuild carries the catalog image cap` (google/gemini-4-argon, catalogMaxImages 10; asserts the onModelChanged-rebuilt model carries maxTokens 65536 AND maxImages 10). --- **vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit** (2026-10-22): Applied in a1287ece02 — the new header now uses the tall style (`testWidgets('…', (` / ` tester,` / `) async {`), matching the rest of the file. --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-22): 🚨 **BLOCKING: the live rebuild still swaps a declared layer the user never edited — the env-preconfig caps (gh-1471 D4)** The previous round's "rebuild must not swap values the user never edited" fix covers the roles-chain layer and the endpoint-detected layer, but not the third declared-caps layer: `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`'s `contextWindow:`/`maxTokens:` (gh-1471 D4). At boot those merge into the resolver's override layer **inside the build only** — they live on the booted `Model` and in no layer this flow reads: - Boot: `buildCliDefaultModel` merges the preconfig caps over the yaml pin per-field (`lib/src/model_roles/provider_catalog.dart:687-709`, doc at `:663-665`; reached via `_buildModel` `bin/fah_model.dart:22-41` ← `bin/fah_runapp.dart:609-618`). - This flow: `_pinnedCaps` (`settings_flow_model_caps.dart:49`) reads only the yaml layer and the process-wide `modelCapabilityOverrides` — the preconfig merge is neither. `_effectiveCapsFor` (`:58-77`) therefore has no preconfig layer, and the PR's own comment promises the opposite: *"a rebuild must never swap values the user did not edit … only the pin's fields move."* Reproduced against this head (scratch probe, modeled on the PR's own live-apply test): a model booted with `contextWindow: 5000` and only a `maxTokens` yaml pin (the exact shape the preconfig build produces); pin **Max output tokens 65536** through the flow → the rebuild swaps the window to the documented `128000` default (`contextWindow 5000` absent, `contextWindow 128000` present in the `/model-edit` print). Two failures in one: 1. **AC3 display** — before any edit the row already reads `Context window — 128000 (catalog)` while the live model carries 5000: the "effective value" the row advertises is not what applies. 2. **AC5 rebuild** — the pin the user made (maxTokens) silently swaps the declared window for the rest of the session; the ctx meter, compaction thresholds and the over-window guard all consume the swapped value. The bench/Docker headless deployments (`FA_PROVIDER_*`) are the shape that boots this way. Fix: give `_effectiveCapsFor` the preconfig layer (e.g. have the boot publish the merged preconfig override into `modelCapabilityOverrides` where the flow's fallback reads it, or thread the preconfig-declared caps through `_pinnedCaps` the way `_currentRoleRef` threads the role layer), plus a regression test booting a preconfigured-window model and pinning an unrelated field. --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-22): ⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the first two context-window presets are below the parse floor — they can never succeed** `_askCapabilityTokens` ports the retired session-only editor's ladder verbatim (`settings_flow_model_caps.dart:271`): ```dart ? const [4096, 8192, 16384, 32768, 65536, 131072, 204800, 1048576] ``` But the persisted write rides the validated upsert, and `ModelCapabilityOverride.fromYaml` rejects anything below the compaction reserve (`capability_resolver.dart:136-141` — `contextWindow must be at least 16384 (the compaction reserve)`). The old editor applied presets via session-only `copyWith` with no floor, so `4K`/`8K` worked there; in the merged surface **4K and 8K are dead rows**: every pick prints `not saved: models.overrides.

..contextWindow must be at least 16384 …` and writes nothing. The PR description advertises the ladder as `context window 4096…1048576`. The failure is graceful (loud error, nothing written), so this is not blocking — but the surface's own AC2 claims working presets. Suggest trimming the context ladder to the floor, e.g. `[16384, 32768, 65536, 131072, 204800, 1048576]` (the maxTokens ladder is fine — its floor is 1024). A test picking the lowest preset would pin the boundary. --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-22): 💡 **SUGGESTION: `_currentRoleRef` matches the first chain entry with this identity — duplicates resolve to the wrong layer** `_currentRoleRef` (`settings_flow_model_caps.dart:27-40`) returns the **first** `ModelRef` on the default chain whose `(provider, modelId)` matches. A roles chain may legally name the same provider/model twice with different explicit caps (fallback entries, a retried endpoint with a different `contextWindow:`); when the serving entry is the second one, the row label and the rebuild read the first entry's caps. Marginal (needs a duplicated identity with divergent caps), and the resolver itself has the same first-match flavor — noting it so the layer-source contract ("display = what applies") stays honest if chains start deduping. --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-22): 🚨 **BLOCKING: live apply resolves caps WITHOUT the role-chain layer — the rebuild can silently swap values the user never edited, and display/apply disagree** `_applyCapabilityEdit` resolves the caps it rebuilds the ACTIVE model from: ```dart final caps = resolveModelCapabilities( provider: provider, modelId: modelId, override: modelCapabilityOverrides?.lookup(provider, modelId), spec: spec, api: spec?.api, reasoning: spec?.reasoning ?? true, ); ``` — no `roleContextWindow`/`roleMaxTokens`/`roleThinkingLevel`. But the resolver's precedence (`capability_resolver.dart`) is **override > role slot > endpoint > remote catalog > spec > default**, and: - the display path this PR adds (`_effectiveCapsFor`, same file) **does** pass the role layers via `_currentRoleRef`, so the row reads `4000 (role override)`; - the boot build path (`buildCatalogModel`, provider_catalog.dart) also passes `roleContextWindow`/`roleMaxTokens`/`roleThinkingLevel`. So the PR's own invariant — "same call shape, same layering — the display can never disagree with the apply" — does not hold for the apply path. Concrete regression (roles chain entry with explicit caps, no pin): 1. `roles: default: [{provider: openai, model: gpt-4o, contextWindow: 4000, maxTokens: 32000}]` → the active model boots with window 4000 (role layer). 2. `/settings` → Model capabilities → openai/gpt-4o → the menu shows `4000 (role override)`. 3. The user pins **Max output tokens 65536** — an edit that does not touch the window. 4. `_applyCapabilityEdit` rebuilds the live model with `contextWindow: caps.contextWindow` where caps resolved **without** the role layer → window becomes the catalog/spec value. The 4000 the menu displayed (and next boot will restore) is silently gone for the rest of the session — the ctx meter, compaction thresholds and the over-window guard all consume it. Same class of loss for the session's endpoint-detected values: `_applyDetectedContextWindow`/`_applyDetectedMaxTokens` put a served window/maxTokens on the live model (and publish `endpointReport` into the registry); any pin on that model rebuilds it from catalog values instead. Fix: resolve the rebuild's caps through the same layering the display uses — pass the `_currentRoleRef(provider, modelId)` layers into this `resolveModelCapabilities` call — and either preserve the current model's endpoint-derived window/maxTokens (the retired `_replaceModelLimits` only ever mutated the edited field via `copyWith`) or re-run detection after the rebuild. Please add a regression test with a roles chain entry carrying explicit caps. --- **vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit** (2026-10-22): Fixed in 5b998561bb, both legs: (a) REBUILD — `_applyCapabilityEdit` now threads the pre-write pin snapshot (`before`) and rebuilds per dimension: a dimension the pin SETS takes the pin's resolved value; a dimension the write UNPINNED re-resolves through the chain (the live model still carries the stale pin — inheriting it would resurrect the un-pinned number); an UNTOUCHED dimension inherits the ACTIVE model's carried value. (b) DISPLAY (the AC3 half of your repro) — `_effectiveCapsFor` falls back to the carried value for a dimension no visible layer names (pin/role/endpoint) on the live identity, and the layer labels name that divergence `carried` (it can only be a boot-injected layer the resolver cannot see — the env-preconfig merge). Your exact repro shape is a regression test: `pinning one field keeps the boot-carried caps of the live model` (model booted with contextWindow 5000 + maxTokens pin; asserts the row reads `5000 (carried)` BEFORE any edit and `/model-edit` shows `contextWindow 5000 · maxTokens 65536` after pinning maxTokens). The unpin path stays chain-resolving: `unpinning drops the stale userPin` still asserts the catalog fallback (128000). --- **vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit** (2026-10-22): Fixed in 5b998561bb: the context ladder is trimmed to the parse floor — `[16384, 32768, 65536, 131072, 204800, 1048576]` (the maxTokens ladder stays; its floor is 1024). Boundary pinned by `the lowest window preset pins exactly the parse floor` (row 1 = 16384 lands the compaction-reserve boundary); the below-floor custom-input test now reaches Custom… at row 7. --- **vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit** (2026-10-22): Rebutting (keeping first-match): the layer-source contract here is "display = what the resolver resolves" — `_currentRoleRef` mirrors the resolver's own first-match-on-identity flavor deliberately, so the label can never contradict what a build through the same chain produces. A chain naming one identity twice with DIVERGENT caps is already ambiguous at the resolver itself (as you note); dedup/last-wins there is the resolver's contract to fix, and this flow would follow it, not fork it. --- **vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit** (2026-10-22): Added in 5b998561bb: `remove (issue #1515 unpin path)` group in test/compaction/context_window_registry_test.dart — drops one identity (windowFor null, isVerified false) while the sibling identity keeps its registration, and remove on an unknown identity is a no-op. ---

- Rebuild — the `*Untouched` gates (`:584-592`): `after?.contextWindow == null && before?.contextWindow == null` — i.e. **the pin doesn't set it**, regardless of role/endpoint naming.

For a dimension named by the roles-chain or the endpoint layer but NOT pinned, where the live model carries a different value, the row displays the chain resolution while the rebuild keeps the carried value — `caps` is computed and then partially ignored, so the same call produces two numbers for one dimension. Reachable state: a dial/copilot session — `_refreshModelCache` applies detection to the live model only for `model.api == 'openai-completions'` (`provider_models.dart:682`), so a fetch populates `_modelContextWindows` without ever applying it; also a degraded-roles boot (chain entry names caps, legacy-built model carries catalog values). No silent swap occurs (the applied value is kept — the safe direction), and the divergence self-heals the moment the user edits that dimension, so this is not blocking.
